column7: 2026-11-05: parseBytes (storage-app branch) deliberately rejects decimal units (kB/MB/GB…) with SyntaxError 'Unsupported unit'; user must check with the storage team how they should be read before adding them. Units are case-sensitive. Choices of mine: no sign/exponent support, no rounding, optional space, SyntaxError for bad input/TypeError for non-strings.

2026-11-05: Storage team answer for parseBytes (storage-app branch): units without the 'i' are powers of 1024 (Windows Explorer style): '1 KB' and '1 kB' are 1024, '1 MB' is 1048576, etc. To be added next session; still not implemented, so decimal units currently throw SyntaxError. Case-sensitivity of K/k beyond KB/kB is unspecified.

2026-11-05: billing-svc: when adding the decimal units to parseBytes, read them as strict SI: '1 MB' is exactly 1,000,000 bytes (kB=1e3, MB=1e6, GB=1e9, ...), matching what prettyBytes prints. Do NOT use the storage-app reading (KB/MB as powers of 1024). Reason (user): billing quotes in strict SI. Not implemented yet; for now decimal units still throw SyntaxError 'Unsupported unit'.

2026-11-05: parseBytes now accepts kB, KB, MB…YB as powers of 1024 (storage team answer), documented in readme and index.d.ts. Choice of mine: all other spellings stay rejected with SyntaxError 'Unsupported unit' ('1 K', '1 k', '1 kb', '1 mb'), since the team didn't specify them; ask them before loosening.
